quiz.title: Module 10: Authentication & Web Security - Comprehensive Assessment

questions.text: What category is currently ranked as the number one web application security risk according to the OWASP Top 10?
questions.explanation: Broken Access Control holds the #1 position in the OWASP Top 10, representing failures to enforce authorization rules on user actions.

questions.text: Why are fast cryptographic hashing algorithms like SHA-256 or MD5 considered unsafe for storing user passwords?

options.text: Modern GPUs can compute billions of fast hashes per second, allowing offline brute-force attacks to crack passwords rapidly.
They cannot be decoded on Linux systems.
They produce hashes that are too long for database strings.
They automatically corrupt user email addresses.

questions.explanation: Fast hashes are designed for high throughput. Password hashing requires adaptive slow hashes (bcrypt, Argon2) to make brute-forcing computationally prohibitive.

questions.text: What are the three components of a JSON Web Token (JWT) separated by periods?
questions.explanation: A JWT consists of Header (algorithm & type), Payload (claims), and Signature (cryptographic verification) separated by dots.

questions.text: Can an attacker read the user data stored inside the Payload of a JWT token transmitted over the network?

options.text: Yes, because the payload is merely Base64URL-encoded (not encrypted); anyone can decode it unless encrypted with JWE.
No, because JWTs are automatically encrypted with AES-256.
Only if they know the secret signing key.

questions.explanation: Standard JWS tokens are signed for integrity, NOT encrypted for confidentiality. The payload is readable by anyone who decodes the Base64URL string.

questions.text: What security flag must be set on an authentication cookie to prevent malicious JavaScript (such as XSS scripts) from accessing document.cookie?
questions.explanation: The httpOnly flag prevents client-side scripts from accessing the cookie via document.cookie, mitigating session hijacking via XSS.

questions.text: What cookie attribute ensures cookies are transmitted strictly across encrypted HTTPS connections and never sent over cleartext HTTP?
questions.explanation: A cookie with the Secure attribute is only sent to the server with an encrypted request over the HTTPS protocol.

questions.text: How does SameSite=Strict on a cookie defend against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks?

options.text: The browser refuses to attach the cookie to any cross-origin HTTP request initiated from an external third-party site.
It encrypts the entire HTTP payload.
It blocks users from clicking external hyperlinks.
It forces the user to solve a CAPTCHA on every request.

questions.explanation: SameSite=Strict ensures the cookie is withheld on all cross-site browsing contexts, preventing malicious sites from executing unauthorized actions.

questions.text: What is the primary difference between Authentication and Authorization?

options.text: Authentication verifies identity (who you are); Authorization verifies permissions (what you are allowed to do).
Authentication happens on the database; Authorization happens in the browser.
Authorization is only needed for financial transactions.

questions.explanation: Authentication proves identity (credentials verification); Authorization determines permissions and access rights (RBAC).

questions.text: What attack occurs when an adversary injects malicious JavaScript into a database, which subsequently executes in the browsers of all other users viewing that record?
questions.explanation: Stored (persistent) XSS occurs when injected script code is permanently stored on the target server (e.g. in a database) and served to victims.

questions.text: How do Parameterized Queries protect SQL databases from SQL Injection attacks?

options.text: They separate user input data from SQL code commands, treating user input purely as literal parameters that cannot alter query structure.
They convert all SQL tables into MongoDB collections.
They delete any queries containing quotation marks.
They run queries on a separate virtual machine.

questions.explanation: Parameterized queries compile the SQL statement template before binding data parameters, making it impossible for input to inject new SQL syntax.

questions.text: What is NoSQL Operator Injection in MongoDB/Express applications?

options.text: When an attacker submits a JSON object containing query operators (like { "$gt": "" }) instead of a string to bypass password checks.
When an attacker deletes the MongoDB configuration file.
When a database runs out of disk storage space.
When an attacker overrides CSS styles with JavaScript.

questions.explanation: If request bodies are not sanitized, attackers can pass MongoDB query operators ($gt, $ne) in place of expected strings to bypass authentication.

questions.text: What header can be removed or disabled via app.disable("x-powered-by") in Express to prevent technology fingerprinting?
questions.explanation: Disabling X-Powered-By removes the header that advertises to scanners that the application is running on Express.

questions.text: What is the role of Helmet middleware in an Express application stack?

options.text: It sets secure HTTP response headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) to shield against common web vulnerabilities.
It compresses static assets using Brotli.
It acts as an automated database backup utility.

questions.explanation: Helmet sets security-focused HTTP headers to protect against clickjacking, sniffing, and cross-site scripting.

questions.text: What is Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) primarily designed to achieve?

options.text: It is a browser security mechanism that restricts web applications from making HTTP requests to a different domain unless authorized by headers.
It is a cloud load balancer algorithm.
It compresses video streams for cellular networks.
It is a database synchronization protocol.

questions.explanation: CORS enables servers to declare which origins are permitted to access their resources from within a browser environment.

questions.text: Why should CORS origin never be configured as wildcard "*" on endpoints that authenticate users with credentials/cookies?

options.text: Browsers block credentialed requests with wildcard origins; allowing all origins enables malicious sites to read authenticated user data.
Wildcards cause high CPU usage in Node.js.
Wildcards only work with HTTP GET.

questions.explanation: Browsers explicitly disallow Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * when Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is true for security reasons.

questions.text: What is the function of Rate Limiting middleware on authentication routes (like /api/login)?

options.text: It throttles and restricts request frequency per IP to prevent automated brute-force password guessing and credential stuffing attacks.
It limits the user to viewing 5 courses per day.
It closes database connection sockets after 10 seconds.

questions.explanation: Rate limiting caps the number of requests an IP can make in a given timeframe, neutralizing automated brute-force scripts.

questions.text: What is an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability?

options.text: When an application exposes direct references to database records (e.g. /api/receipts/1042) without verifying if the requesting user owns that record.
When an object has no JavaScript methods.
When a database table has no primary key.
When a CSS stylesheet has broken image links.

questions.explanation: IDOR occurs when user-supplied input is used to access objects directly without an authorization check verifying ownership.

questions.text: In JWT token architecture, why is the dual-token pattern (short-lived Access Token + long-lived Refresh Token) recommended?

options.text: If an access token is intercepted, its damage window is limited to minutes; refresh tokens can be revoked in the database upon security alerts.
Because single tokens cannot store strings.
To allow users to log in without a password.
It is required by the HTTP/1.1 specification.

questions.explanation: Short-lived access tokens minimize exposure if stolen, while revocable refresh tokens provide seamless re-authentication without frequent logins.

questions.text: What security header instructs web browsers to only communicate with a domain over HTTPS and never use unencrypted HTTP for future requests?
questions.explanation: HSTS ensures browsers automatically upgrade all future requests to HTTPS, preventing SSL-stripping man-in-the-middle attacks.

questions.text: What does a Content Security Policy (CSP) header control in web browsers?

options.text: It defines an allowlist of approved domains and protocols from which scripts, styles, images, and fonts are permitted to load and execute.
It limits the number of CSS classes on a page.
It forces search engines to index images.
It verifies user passwords with the server.

questions.explanation: CSP is an effective defense-in-depth standard that restricts which scripts, styles, and assets the browser is allowed to fetch and run.

lessons.content:
# Professional Git Workflows: Branching Strategies, Pull Requests & Merge Conflicts

## 1. Overview & Learning Objectives
Git is the universal distributed version control system for software development. In this lesson, you will master:
- Feature Branch and Trunk-Based development workflows.
- Merging strategies: Merge Commit (`git merge`), Fast-Forward, and Squash Merging.
- Resolving complex three-way merge conflicts.
- Interactive rebasing (`git rebase -i`) for clean, atomic commit histories.

---

## 2. Resolving Merge Conflicts Cleanly
A merge conflict occurs when two branches modify the exact same lines of code:

```
<<<<<<< HEAD (Current Branch - main)
const API_BASE_URL = 'https://api.redkross.org.in/v2';
=======
const API_BASE_URL = 'https://api-staging.redkross.org.in/v2';
>>>>>>> feature/telemetry-upgrade (Incoming Branch)
```

Resolution steps:
1. Examine both implementations and consult with collaborating developers.
2. Manually edit the file to preserve the correct unified logic.
3. Remove the conflict marker lines (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`).
4. Stage and commit:
```bash
git add src/config/api.js
git commit -m "fix(config): resolve API endpoint conflict between main and staging"
```

---

## 3. Key Takeaways
- Never commit secrets or `.env` files to Git repositories; always maintain a strict `.gitignore`.
- Keep commits small, focused, and atomic with conventional commit messages (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`).

## 4. Documentation & References
- [Git Pro Book (Official)](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2)

lessons.content:
# Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) with GitHub Actions

## 1. Overview & Learning Objectives
Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Deployment (CD) automate testing and deployment on every code commit. In this lesson, you will master:
- Creating GitHub Actions workflow manifests in `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`.
- Triggers: `push` to `main`, `pull_request`, and manual dispatch.
- Matrix builds across multiple Node versions.
- Storing and referencing encrypted repository secrets (`secrets.DATABASE_URL`, `secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN`).

---

## 2. Production CI/CD Workflow Manifest (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
```yaml
name: RedKross Academy CI/CD Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  audit-and-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout Source Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js Runtime
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Deterministic Dependency Install
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint Code Quality
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Run Automated Test Suites
        run: npm test

      - name: Build Production Distribution
        run: npm run build
```

---

## 3. Key Takeaways
- Branch protection rules in GitHub should mandate that the CI pipeline passes before a pull request can be merged into `main`.
- Never expose API keys or passwords in workflow files; always inject them via GitHub Repository Secrets.

## 4. Documentation & References
- [GitHub Actions Documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions)

lessons.content:
# Containerizing Full Stack Applications with Docker & Docker Compose

## 1. Overview & Learning Objectives
"It works on my machine" is solved by containerization. Docker bundles an application with its runtime, system tools, and libraries into a portable image. In this lesson, you will master:
- Docker concepts: Images vs Containers.
- Writing multi-stage production Dockerfiles to minimize image size (<150MB).
- Managing multi-container applications (Node.js API + MongoDB) with `docker-compose.yml`.
- Persistent data volumes for databases.

---

## 2. Multi-Stage Production Dockerfile
```dockerfile
# Stage 1: Build & Dependencies
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

# Stage 2: Lean Production Runtime (<150MB)
FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=builder /app/server ./server

USER node
EXPOSE 4000
CMD ["node", "server/index.js"]
```

---

## 3. Docker Compose Orchestration (docker-compose.yml)
```yaml
version: '3.8'

services:
  api:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "4000:4000"
    environment:
      - PORT=4000
      - MONGO_URI=mongodb://mongo:27017/redkross_academy
    depends_on:
      - mongo

  mongo:
    image: mongo:7.0
    ports:
      - "27017:27017"
    volumes:
      - mongo_data:/data/db

volumes:
  mongo_data:
```

---

## 4. Key Takeaways
- Multi-stage builds keep development dependencies, build compilers, and source code out of the final production image.
- Always run Docker containers as non-root users (`USER node`) for container security.

## 5. Documentation & References
- [Docker Official Documentation](https://docs.docker.com/)

lessons.content:
# Production Deployment & Cloud Hosting: Vercel, Railway, Cloudflare Tunnels & Nginx

## 1. Overview & Learning Objectives
Deploying to production requires understanding DNS routing, SSL certificate automation, reverse proxies, and serverless hosting platforms. In this lesson, you will master:
- Serverless edge deployment on **Vercel** with custom domains.
- Managed container hosting on **Railway** and **Render**.
- Self-hosted infrastructure using **Nginx** reverse proxies and Let's Encrypt SSL.
- Exposing private self-hosted servers securely using **Cloudflare Tunnels** without opening public inbound firewall ports.

---

## 2. Cloudflare Tunnel Architecture
Traditional web hosting requires port forwarding (Port 80/443) and static public IP addresses. Cloudflare Tunnels (`cloudflared`) establish an encrypted, outbound-only connection to Cloudflare's global edge network:

```
[ User Browser ]
       |
       | HTTPS (Anycast Edge, DDoS Mitigation, WAF)
       v
[ Cloudflare Global Edge Network ]
       |
       | Encrypted Outbound-Only Tunnel (QUIC / HTTP/2)
       v
[ Local cloudflared Daemon ] (Inside private server / localhost)
       |
       | Localhost loopback
       v
[ Node.js Application / Nginx ] (Port 3000 / 4000)
```

---

## 3. Production Readiness Checklist
Before launching an application to live users, verify:
1. All database passwords and API keys are stored in environment variables (`.env`).
2. SSL/TLS is strictly enforced with automatic HTTP -> HTTPS redirects.
3. Automated database backups are scheduled.
4. Process managers (PM2 / systemd / Docker) are configured with automatic restart on crash policies (`restart: always`).

---

## 4. Key Takeaways
- Cloudflare Tunnels eliminate the risk of direct-to-IP DDoS attacks by completely closing all incoming firewall ports.
- Vercel provides zero-configuration Git-based CI/CD deployment with preview environments for pull requests.

## 5. Documentation & References
- [Vercel Deployment Documentation](https://vercel.com/docs)
- [Cloudflare Tunnel Documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/)

questions.text: What Git command allows interactively squashing, editing, and reorganizing past commits into a clean, atomic commit history?
questions.explanation: Interactive rebasing (git rebase -i) opens an editor to squash, reorder, reword, or drop commits before merging into main.

questions.text: In the Software Testing Pyramid, which tier of tests should form the largest, fastest foundation of your automated test suite?
questions.explanation: Unit tests are fast to run and isolated, providing the broad base of the testing pyramid.

questions.text: What guiding philosophy defines React Testing Library (RTL)?

options.text: The more your tests resemble the way your software is used, the more confidence they can give you.
Always test internal state variables directly.
All tests must be written in Python.

questions.explanation: RTL encourages testing from the user perspective (querying by accessible roles, labels, text) rather than testing internal state implementation.

questions.text: What query method is recommended as top priority when searching for elements in React Testing Library?
questions.explanation: getByRole queries elements exposed to the accessibility tree, reflecting how assistive technologies and users perceive the UI.

questions.text: What library is standard for making simulated HTTP assertions against Express applications without binding to live network ports in integration tests?
questions.explanation: Supertest provides high-level HTTP abstractions for testing Node.js HTTP servers without opening actual network ports.

questions.text: In GitHub Actions, where are workflow YAML files required to be located within a repository?
questions.explanation: GitHub Actions searches for workflow files defined in the .github/workflows directory of the repository.

questions.text: What is the primary benefit of Multi-Stage Builds in Dockerfile design?

options.text: They separate build tools and devDependencies into a temporary builder container, producing a clean, minimal runtime image (<150MB).
They install multiple operating systems in one image.
They run containers faster on GPU chips.
They eliminate the need for Docker Compose.

questions.explanation: Multi-stage builds leave compilers, source code, and node_modules out of the final layer, drastically reducing container size and attack surface.

questions.text: What file prevents build artifacts, secret .env files, and node_modules from being copied into a Docker build context?
questions.explanation: .dockerignore prevents files and directories from being included in the Docker build context, speeding up builds and preventing secret leaks.

questions.text: What tool orchestrates and configures multi-container Docker applications (such as a Node.js API container + a MongoDB container)?
questions.explanation: Docker Compose uses a YAML file (docker-compose.yml) to configure application services, networks, and persistent data volumes.

questions.text: How does a Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared) enhance the security of a self-hosted web server?

options.text: It creates an outbound-only encrypted tunnel to Cloudflare's edge, allowing you to host web services without opening ANY inbound ports on your firewall.
It encrypts the server's RAM hardware.
It replaces the Linux operating system.
It automatically translates English to Spanish.

questions.explanation: Cloudflare Tunnels establish an outbound connection to Cloudflare edge nodes, routing traffic without exposing public IPs or opening inbound router ports.

questions.text: What command is used to stage resolved merge conflicts after manually editing conflict markers in code files?
questions.explanation: After resolving conflict markers in files, running git add stages the resolved content, ready for a completion commit.

questions.text: What Vitest / Jest matcher verifies that a mock function was called exactly twice during a test execution?
questions.explanation: toHaveBeenCalledTimes(number) asserts that a spy or mock function was called the exact specified number of times.

questions.text: Why is it critical to create a non-root user (e.g. USER node) in production Dockerfiles?

options.text: Running as root in a container increases risk; if an attacker escapes the container, they gain root privileges on the host server.
Containers cannot run Node.js as root.
It is required by the npm registry.

questions.explanation: Following least privilege by switching to a non-root user (USER node) mitigates severe container-breakout vulnerabilities.

questions.text: What Git command allows applying a specific commit from one branch onto your current branch without merging the entire branch?
questions.explanation: git cherry-pick applies the changes introduced by some existing commits onto the current active HEAD branch.

questions.text: What is the purpose of test coverage reporting in Continuous Integration pipelines?

options.text: It quantifies the percentage of lines, functions, branches, and statements executed during automated test runs.
It measures the speed of developer typing.
It counts how many users have logged into the app.

questions.explanation: Test coverage tools (like c8 / Istanbul) report which portions of the codebase are exercised by test suites to highlight unverified logic.

questions.text: What feature in GitHub allows teams to prevent unreviewed or failing code from being merged directly into the main production branch?
questions.explanation: Branch protection rules require status checks (passing CI) and pull request reviews before branches can be merged into main.

questions.text: What is the function of a Reverse Proxy (like Nginx) positioned in front of a Node.js application server?

options.text: It terminates SSL/TLS, buffers slow clients, serves static assets directly, and load-balances requests across multiple Node worker instances.
It compiles React code to assembly language.

questions.explanation: Nginx acts as a high-performance reverse proxy that handles TLS termination, gzip compression, static file caching, and request forwarding.

questions.text: What Docker command lists all currently running containers along with their status, container ID, and port bindings?
questions.explanation: docker ps shows active running containers, their ports, names, and uptime.

questions.text: What is the role of an automated End-to-End (E2E) testing framework like Playwright or Cypress?

options.text: It launches real headless browsers and simulates complete end-user journeys (logging in, submitting forms, taking exams) across the full stack.
It tests single JavaScript math functions in isolation.
It scans hard drives for malware.

questions.explanation: E2E testing tools run real browser sessions and verify that the combined frontend, backend, and database function seamlessly together.

questions.text: What happens when a process manager like PM2 is configured with autorestart: true in a production Node.js deployment?

options.text: If the Node application encounters an uncaught exception and crashes, PM2 immediately spawns a fresh process to restore uptime without manual intervention.
It restarts the server computer every hour.
It sends an SMS to all registered users.

questions.explanation: PM2 monitors the Node.js process and automatically restarts it upon unexpected crashes, maintaining high service availability.

# Capstone Architecture & Specifications: Full Stack Course Management System

## 1. Overview & Learning Objectives
The Capstone Project synthesizes every discipline covered in this 12-week curriculum. You will architect and build a complete **Course & Certification Management System**:
- Three-tier decoupled architecture: React 18 Frontend, Express.js Backend API, and persistent Database.
- Strict Zero-Blue institutional cyber aesthetic (`#65F58A` Emerald, `#071018` Deep Cyber Void).
- Real-time bidirectional WebSockets for instant admin-to-student telemetry.
- Cryptographically verifiable PDF credential generation.

---

## 2. System Architecture Blueprint
```
[ STUDENT CLIENT (React 18) ] <====== WebSocket (Socket.io) ======> [ SUPER ADMIN STUDIO (React 18) ]
              \                                                               /
               \                                                             /
                \                         HTTP REST API                     /
                 +=========================> [ EXPRESS.JS API ] <==========+
                                                    |
                                            (JWT / RBAC / Zod)
                                                    |
                                        +-----------+-----------+
                                        |                       |
                                        v                       v
                              [ POSTGRESQL / MONGO ]    [ CLOUD STORAGE ]
                              (Courses, Enrolments)     (PDFs, Video Streams)
```

---

## 3. Key Deliverables
1. **Course Directory & Detail Pages:** Filterable courses with enrollment triggers.
2. **Interactive CBT Exam Engine:** Split-view questions palette, live decrementing attempts (3 -> 2 -> 1), and 24-hour proctoring lockouts.
3. **Admin Curriculum Studio:** 4-step wizard to create, edit, and reorder modules, lessons, and MCQs.
4. **Verifiable PDF Credential:** High-res institutional certificate with verification hashes.

## 4. Documentation & References
- [Full Stack Architecture Blueprint](https://github.com/Atharv-design/redkross-academy)

# Frontend Architecture: State Management, Component Hierarchy & Protected Routing

## 1. Overview & Learning Objectives
A scalable frontend requires clean directory structure and decoupled state. In this lesson, you will master:
- Component hierarchy: Common, Layout, Public, Student, and Admin pages.
- Global authentication context (`AuthContext`) with LocalStorage fallback.
- Client-side routing with role-based Route Guards.
- Enforcing the strict Zero-Blue institutional design tokens.

---

## 2. Component Hierarchy Blueprint
```
src/
  ├── components/
  │    ├── common/ (Navbar, Footer, Modal)
  │    ├── student/ (ExamCBTInterface, PDFCertificateModal)
  │    └── ui/ (PixelBackground, CyberCards)
  ├── pages/
  │    ├── public/ (HomePage, CourseCatalogPage, CourseDetailPage)
  │    ├── student/ (StudentDashboardPage, LessonPlayerPage)
  │    └── admin/ (AdminDashboardPage, AdminCoursesPage)
  ├── services/
  │    ├── api/ (apiClient)
  │    └── db/ (mockEngine, videoStorage)
```

---

## 3. Key Takeaways
- Centralize all API network calls inside an `apiClient` abstraction to easily switch between mock engines and live PostgreSQL.
- Keep layout components focused on styling, delegating logic to custom hooks.

## 4. Documentation & References
- [React Architecture Best Practices](https://react.dev/learn/scaling-up-with-reducer-and-context)

# Production Hardening, Performance Audits (Lighthouse 95+), Security Review & Final Launch

## 1. Overview & Learning Objectives
The final step in professional engineering is production hardening and launch verification. In this lesson, you will master:
- Running Google Lighthouse audits to achieve 95+ scores across Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO.
- Vite bundle analysis and code-splitting optimizations.
- Final security verification: checking for exposed secrets, missing headers, or unhandled errors.
- Final launch readiness sign-off.

---

## 2. Lighthouse 95+ Optimization Checklist
- [x] **Performance (95+):**
  - Next-gen image formats (AVIF/WebP) with explicit `width` and `height`.
  - Minified CSS and JavaScript chunks with Gzip/Brotli compression.
  - Zero render-blocking resources in the document `<head>`.
- [x] **Accessibility (100):**
  - Minimum 4.5:1 color contrast ratio across all text elements.
  - High-visibility keyboard `:focus-visible` indicators on interactive elements.
  - Complete semantic landmark structure (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<footer>`).
- [x] **Best Practices (100):**
  - HTTPS enforced with strict HSTS.
  - No vulnerable npm packages (`npm audit` clean).
  - Clean console output with zero runtime errors.
- [x] **SEO (100):**
  - Canonical URL declared on all pages.
  - Meta description and Open Graph cards configured.

---

## 3. Launch Verification Protocol
Execute final end-to-end integration test suites:
```bash
# 1. Run full unit and integration tests
npm test

# 2. Build production distribution
npm run build

# 3. Test production preview build
npm run preview
```

---

## 4. Key Takeaways
- High-craft engineering means testing every single user flow before declaring a system complete.
- Continuous monitoring and audit logging ensure operational integrity long after launch.

## 5. Documentation & References
- [Google Lighthouse Documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview/)
- [Web.dev Performance Auditing Guide](https://web.dev/fast/)

questions.text: In a modern full stack MERN application, what is the role of the REST API application server?

options.text: It handles business logic, authenticates requests, enforces authorization (RBAC), and orchestrates database transactions between client and database.
It serves strictly as a static CSS file CDN.
It runs inside the user's browser sandbox.
It replaces the browser rendering engine.

questions.explanation: The backend API acts as the secure intermediary, executing business logic, enforcing validation, and interacting with the database.

questions.text: What protocol is utilized by Socket.io to establish low-latency, bidirectional, real-time communication between browser clients and servers?
questions.explanation: Socket.io primarily uses WebSockets for bidirectional low-latency communication, gracefully falling back to HTTP long-polling when needed.

questions.text: Why is generating vector PDF certificates client-side using jsPDF preferable over returning rasterized screenshot images?

options.text: Vector PDFs preserve crisp, resolution-independent fonts, sharp vector vector borders, selectable text, and smaller file sizes (<100KB).
Raster images cannot be opened on mobile phones.
jsPDF automatically encrypts the student's hard drive.

questions.explanation: Vector graphics and native font glyphs in PDFs scale cleanly to any resolution or print size without pixelation or heavy image byte bloat.

questions.text: When a Super Admin deletes a course in the Admin Studio, why must database cascading deletion rules be executed?

options.text: To cleanly remove all associated child modules, lessons, quizzes, questions, options, and student enrolments, preventing orphaned records and broken foreign keys.
To delete all user accounts in the system.
It is a requirement of HTML5 validation.

questions.explanation: Cascading deletes maintain referential integrity by cleaning up all subordinate records that depend on the deleted parent course entity.

questions.text: What score target across Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO is required to meet high-craft production standards?

options.text: Scores do not matter in production.
Lighthouse audits only measure CSS animations.

questions.explanation: Production-grade applications target 95+ across all Lighthouse categories, guaranteeing optimal speed, universal access, and discoverability.

questions.text: In the CBT Exam Interface, why should question attempts decrement live (3 -> 2 -> 1) with an automatic 24-hour lockout when exhausted?

options.text: To enforce rigorous academic evaluation integrity, preventing brute-force guessing and enforcing a mandatory study cooldown.
Because servers cannot process more than 3 requests.
To delete student accounts after 3 tries.
To force students to purchase new computers.

questions.explanation: Limiting attempts and enforcing a 24-hour cooldown prevents trial-and-error guessing on certification assessments and encourages thorough review.

questions.text: What is the role of a Unique Verification ID (e.g. RK-XXXX-XXXX) printed on an academic certificate?

options.text: It enables employers and external third parties to query the public registry and verify that the credential was genuinely issued to that candidate.
It is the student's credit card number.
It specifies the student's IP address.

questions.explanation: Unique verification IDs map to tamper-proof credential records in the database, allowing cryptographic verification on the public registry.

questions.text: How does Socket.io ensure that when an admin deletes or creates a course, student catalog pages update instantly without needing a manual browser refresh?

options.text: The admin action triggers an event emission (e.g. io.emit("course:mutation")) which client listeners intercept to refetch data immediately.
The server reboots all student computers.
The browser runs a continuous infinite while loop.
Students must refresh the page manually.

questions.explanation: WebSocket push events deliver instant notification of mutations to all active connected clients, triggering real-time UI updates.

questions.text: What design token colors are strictly mandated to enforce the RedKross Academy Zero-Blue cyber aesthetic?

options.text: Emerald Green (#65F58A), Mint (#35E6B5), and Deep Cyber Void (#071018 / #092218) with 0% Blue.

questions.explanation: The RedKross Academy brand strictly enforces a zero-blue cyber design system built around emerald green, mint, and deep dark green surfaces.

questions.text: What should be displayed on the student public catalog when the Super Admin toggles the catalog release status to EMBARGOED?

options.text: A clean preparation empty-state screen stating "Curriculum Preparation in Progress (Courses will be out soon)", hiding all courses from unauthenticated visitors.

questions.explanation: When embargoed, public visitors see the refined "Courses will be out soon" state, preventing premature access to unreleased curriculum.

questions.text: What tool should you use to verify that a client-side bundle does not accidentally include heavy, bloated libraries before deploying to production?
questions.explanation: Bundle visualizers produce interactive treemaps of output chunks, identifying oversized dependencies for code-splitting.

questions.text: In the CBT Exam Question Palette, what visual marking immediately informs the student whether a question has been answered or not?

options.text: Attempted questions are marked in Green (#65F58A); Not Attempted questions are marked in Red (#F43F5E).
Attempted questions are hidden from the grid.

questions.explanation: The question palette color-codes answered questions in green and unattempted questions in red for instant test progress visibility.

questions.text: What happens when a student attempts to switch browser tabs or loses window focus during an active proctored examination?

options.text: The anti-cheat proctoring protocol immediately intercepts the focus loss, terminates the exam session, and enforces a mandatory 24-hour lockout.

questions.explanation: Anti-cheat monitors visibilitychange and blur events; detecting tab switching immediately records a violation and locks the exam for 24 hours.

questions.text: What HTTP status code should the backend return if an unauthorized student attempts to trigger an administrative course deletion endpoint?
questions.explanation: 403 Forbidden indicates that the server understands the request but refuses to authorize it because the user lacks required permissions.

questions.text: Why should database credentials and JWT signing secrets never be hardcoded into Git source code repositories?

options.text: Any collaborator or attacker with repository access can extract secrets and completely compromise database clusters and counterfeit signed tokens.
Git cannot commit strings containing punctuation.
Hardcoded secrets slow down network bandwidth.
It prevents the code from compiling in React.

questions.explanation: Hardcoding secrets exposes credentials to anyone with code access; secrets must always be injected at runtime via environment variables.

questions.text: In the Open edX-style lesson player, how is sequential module gating enforced?

options.text: Module N+1 remains locked until all mandatory lessons in Module N are completed AND the Module N technical assessment is passed with >= 80%.
All modules are completely unlocked from day one.
Modules unlock based on calendar dates only.
Students must pay money to unlock each module.

questions.explanation: Sequential gating enforces that students master each module by completing all lessons and passing the assessment before unlocking subsequent modules.

questions.text: What format should technical documentation and lesson instructional notes be stored in to allow rich styling, code blocks, and diagrams?
questions.explanation: Markdown allows authors to write structured content with headings, lists, tables, and syntax-highlighted code blocks rendered into HTML.

questions.text: What is the function of the lead_author object stored on a course record in the database?

options.text: It encapsulates the instructor's name, title, role, and avatar to present verifiable educator provenance on course detail views.
It stores the author's bank account details.
It locks the course from being edited.
It is used to send marketing emails.

questions.explanation: lead_author attributes the curriculum to a recognized industry educator with credentials and institutional title.

questions.text: How does the Super Admin confirm course creation in the Admin Studio?

options.text: Clicking "Save & Finalize Course" persists the course hierarchy to the database and displays a celebratory emerald pop-up modal with direct links to view in catalog and student portal.
The admin must restart the computer.
An alert prompt asks for a root password.

questions.explanation: The course builder persists deep modules and questions, then renders an elegant success modal with confetti and direct navigation actions.

questions.text: What is the ultimate objective of completing the Full Stack Web Development curriculum?

options.text: To achieve complete mastery of end-to-end web engineering, from foundational protocols and UI craft through scalable APIs, security defense, and automated cloud deployments.
To learn how to use a computer mouse.
To memorize basic HTML tags only.

questions.explanation: The curriculum equips candidates with comprehensive full stack engineering skills spanning frontend, backend, security, testing, and deployment.

questions.text: What is the primary role of the Domain Name System (DNS) in web networking?

options.text: Encrypting HTTP request payloads with TLS certificates
Translating human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses
Serving static HTML documents directly to the client browser
Balancing server CPU utilization across cluster nodes

questions.explanation: DNS functions as the phonebook of the internet, resolving human-readable hostnames (such as redkross.org.in) into routable IP addresses (such as 198.51.100.42).

questions.text: Which protocol handles the reliable transmission of web packets by establishing a 3-way handshake prior to data exchange?
questions.explanation: TCP guarantees ordered, error-checked delivery of packets between client and server by completing a SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK handshake.

questions.text: In the HTTP/1.1 protocol, which status code class specifically represents client-side errors such as unauthorized access or missing resources?
questions.explanation: 4xx status codes (e.g. 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found) designate client-side errors.

questions.text: What default port is used for encrypted HTTPS communication across the public internet?
questions.explanation: Standard unencrypted HTTP traffic operates on port 80, whereas TLS-encrypted HTTPS traffic defaults to port 443.

questions.text: What is the semantic purpose of the HTML5 <main> element?

options.text: To wrap the global site header, navigation bar, and primary logo
To encapsulate the dominant, unique content of the document body
To contain site-wide copyright notices and privacy policy links
To render supplementary sidebar navigation menus

questions.explanation: The <main> tag represents the central content unique to the document, excluding headers, footers, and sidebars.

questions.text: How many visible <main> landmark elements should be present in a valid HTML5 document?
questions.explanation: W3C specifications mandate that an HTML document must have only one non-hidden <main> element to provide an unambiguous landmark for screen readers.

questions.text: Which HTML5 element represents a self-contained, independently distributable piece of content such as a blog post or news story?
questions.explanation: An <article> represents a self-contained composition in a document that is independently reusable, such as a forum post or magazine article.

questions.text: Why should external links targeting new tabs (target="_blank") always include rel="noopener noreferrer"?

options.text: To prevent the new page from accessing window.opener and performing reverse tabnabbing attacks
To force the browser to preload the external domain DNS cache
To compress images downloaded from the linked domain
To disable JavaScript in the destination tab

questions.explanation: Adding rel="noopener" ensures the new window runs in a separate process and cannot manipulate window.opener to redirect the originating page to a phishing site.

questions.text: Which selector combination possesses the highest specificity weight according to standard W3C cascade rules?
questions.explanation: #main-nav a.active contains 1 ID, 1 Class, and 1 Element (0, 1, 1, 1), which easily overrides any number of classes or elements without an ID.

questions.text: What is the primary benefit of declaring * { box-sizing: border-box; } across a project stylesheet?

options.text: It forces borders to render using hardware-accelerated SVG vectors.
Element padding and border widths are absorbed inside the declared width, preventing layout overflow.
It prevents all margin collapsing in the vertical flow.
It enables CSS Grid auto-placement on inline elements.

questions.explanation: border-box causes the specified width and height to include the content, padding, and border, dramatically simplifying responsive layout math.

questions.text: When flex-direction is configured as row, which axis does justify-content align items along?
questions.explanation: justify-content always aligns items along the Main Axis, which runs horizontally when flex-direction is row (or row-reverse).

questions.text: What CSS Grid declaration creates an auto-responsive grid where cards wrap into columns of at least 250px without requiring media queries?
questions.explanation: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)) dynamically fills available width with as many 250px+ columns as can fit and stretches them equally.

questions.text: What error is thrown when code attempts to access a variable declared with let or const prior to its initialization line?

options.text: ReferenceError: Cannot access variable before initialization

questions.explanation: Accessing a let or const variable within its Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) before evaluation throws a ReferenceError.

questions.text: What is the output of typeof null according to standard JavaScript specifications?
questions.explanation: Due to a historical legacy bug in the original 1995 JavaScript implementation, typeof null evaluates to "object".

questions.text: What is the difference between null and undefined in JavaScript?

options.text: undefined represents uninitialized variable state, while null represents intentional assignment of no value.
null is a primitive type, while undefined is an object.
undefined throws an error when converted to boolean.
There is no difference; they are exact aliases.

questions.explanation: undefined signifies that a variable has been declared but not assigned; null is an explicit assignment indicating the absence of any object value.

questions.text: How does the Nullish Coalescing Operator (??) differ from the Logical OR Operator (||)?

options.text: ?? evaluates right-hand operands only when the left-hand operand is null or undefined, preserving 0, false, and empty strings.
?? mutates the left-hand variable in place.

questions.explanation: The logical OR operator (||) falls back on any falsy value (including 0, false, and ""), whereas ?? only triggers for nullish values (null or undefined).

questions.text: In the JavaScript Event Loop, which queue is prioritized and completely drained before the next Macrotask is executed?
questions.explanation: The event loop processes all pending jobs in the microtask queue to completion before picking the next macrotask from the task queue.

questions.text: What will be the output order of: console.log("A"); setTimeout(() => console.log("B"), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("C")); console.log("D"); ?
questions.explanation: A and D execute synchronously. Promise microtask C executes immediately after synchronous code. setTimeout macrotask B runs in the next loop tick.

questions.text: How does Promise.allSettled() differ fundamentally from Promise.all()?

options.text: Promise.allSettled() waits for all promises to settle and never rejects, returning an array of status objects.
Promise.allSettled() rejects if any single promise rejects.
Promise.allSettled() only executes on node.js backends.
Promise.allSettled() executes promises sequentially instead of in parallel.

questions.explanation: Promise.all fails fast on the first rejection. Promise.allSettled waits for all input promises to settle, returning { status, value/reason } for each.

questions.text: What is the modern native browser API method used to perform a true deep copy of a nested JavaScript object?
questions.explanation: structuredClone() is the standard native deep-cloning algorithm, accurately copying nested objects, arrays, Dates, and Maps.

questions.text: What is the primary role of the key prop when rendering arrays of components in React?

options.text: To encrypt component props in memory
To help React's reconciliation algorithm identify which items have changed, been added, or been removed
To bind the component to a database primary key
To apply unique CSS styling to each item

questions.explanation: Keys provide a stable identity to array elements, enabling the diffing algorithm to reuse DOM nodes efficiently across renders.

questions.text: Why does mutating React state directly (e.g. user.name = "Alex") fail to trigger a visual component re-render?

options.text: React relies on Object.is identity comparison; mutating an object in place preserves the same memory reference, causing React to skip rendering.
Direct mutation crashes the browser JavaScript engine.
React components only re-render on mouse movement.
The browser DOM blocks all direct variable edits.

questions.explanation: React checks if the new state reference is different from the old reference using Object.is. In-place mutations maintain identical references.

questions.text: When does the cleanup function returned from a useEffect hook execute?

options.text: Only when the browser window closes.
Immediately before the component unmounts, and before every re-execution of the effect when dependencies change.
Every time the user clicks a button.

questions.explanation: The cleanup function runs when the component unmounts and prior to running the effect again on dependency updates, cleaning up previous side effects.

questions.text: How does updating a useRef object (e.g. ref.current = 10) differ from updating a useState value?

options.text: Mutating ref.current does NOT trigger a component re-render; updating state DOES trigger a re-render.
useRef can only store strings, while useState stores objects.
useRef values are wiped on every re-render.
useState cannot be used inside functional components.

questions.explanation: useRef stores a mutable value across renders without triggering a re-render when mutated.

questions.text: Which underlying C++ library provides the event loop, cross-platform asynchronous I/O, and the default worker thread pool in Node.js?
questions.explanation: libuv is the multi-platform C library that powers the Node.js event loop, asynchronous socket abstraction, and thread pool.

questions.text: By default, how many worker threads are allocated in the libuv thread pool for handling filesystem and DNS operations?
questions.explanation: libuv defaults to a pool of 4 worker threads, which can be tuned using the UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE environment variable.

questions.text: Why should you avoid using synchronous filesystem methods (such as fs.readFileSync) in a production web server?

options.text: They block the single Node.js main thread entirely, preventing all other concurrent requests from being processed until the disk read finishes.
They only work on Linux operating systems.

questions.explanation: Because Node.js runs on a single main thread for JavaScript execution, synchronous calls block that thread and freeze all concurrent user requests.

questions.text: What Node.js core module is specifically designed to safely handle and normalize file and directory paths across different operating systems?
questions.explanation: node:path provides utilities for working with file and directory paths, resolving Windows backslash and POSIX slash discrepancies.

questions.text: What middleware function must be mounted in Express to parse incoming JSON request payloads into req.body?
questions.explanation: express.json() is the built-in middleware based on body-parser that parses incoming requests with JSON payloads.

questions.text: How does Express identify a global error-handling middleware function compared to regular middleware?

options.text: It has exactly 4 parameters: (err, req, res, next)
It must be written in TypeScript

questions.explanation: Express inspects function.length; error-handling middleware is defined with four arguments (err, req, res, next).

questions.text: What HTTP status code should be returned when a new resource is successfully created via a POST request?
questions.explanation: HTTP status code 201 Created indicates that the request has succeeded and led to the creation of a new resource.

questions.text: What is an Idempotent HTTP method in REST architecture?

options.text: A method where multiple identical requests have the exact same side effect on server state as a single request (e.g. GET, PUT, DELETE).
A method that executes in under 1 millisecond.
A method that requires no authorization.
A method that only transmits XML payloads.

questions.explanation: An HTTP method is idempotent if the intended effect on the server of making multiple identical requests is the same as making a single request.

questions.text: What binary format does MongoDB use internally to store documents with support for rich data types like Date and ObjectId?
questions.explanation: MongoDB stores data in BSON (Binary JSON) format, extending JSON with types like ObjectId, Date, Binary data, and Decimal128.

questions.text: What is the maximum document size limit enforced by MongoDB for a single BSON document?
questions.explanation: The maximum BSON document size is 16MB to prevent unbounded document growth from degrading RAM and network performance.

questions.text: What update operator must be used in MongoDB to update specific fields in a document without replacing the entire document?
questions.explanation: The $set operator replaces the value of a field with the specified value without replacing the surrounding document.

questions.text: Which atomic operator increments the numerical value of a field in a MongoDB document by a specified amount?
questions.explanation: The $inc operator increments a field by a specified value, e.g. { $inc: { enrolled: 1 } }.

questions.text: What category is currently ranked as the number one web application security risk according to the OWASP Top 10?
questions.explanation: Broken Access Control holds the #1 position in the OWASP Top 10, representing failures to enforce authorization rules on user actions.

questions.text: Why are fast cryptographic hashing algorithms like SHA-256 or MD5 considered unsafe for storing user passwords?

options.text: Modern GPUs can compute billions of fast hashes per second, allowing offline brute-force attacks to crack passwords rapidly.
They cannot be decoded on Linux systems.
They produce hashes that are too long for database strings.
They automatically corrupt user email addresses.

questions.explanation: Fast hashes are designed for high throughput. Password hashing requires adaptive slow hashes (bcrypt, Argon2) to make brute-forcing computationally prohibitive.

questions.text: What are the three components of a JSON Web Token (JWT) separated by periods?
questions.explanation: A JWT consists of Header (algorithm & type), Payload (claims), and Signature (cryptographic verification) separated by dots.

questions.text: Can an attacker read the user data stored inside the Payload of a JWT token transmitted over the network?

options.text: Yes, because the payload is merely Base64URL-encoded (not encrypted); anyone can decode it unless encrypted with JWE.
No, because JWTs are automatically encrypted with AES-256.
Only if they know the secret signing key.

questions.explanation: Standard JWS tokens are signed for integrity, NOT encrypted for confidentiality. The payload is readable by anyone who decodes the Base64URL string.

questions.text: What Git command allows interactively squashing, editing, and reorganizing past commits into a clean, atomic commit history?
questions.explanation: Interactive rebasing (git rebase -i) opens an editor to squash, reorder, reword, or drop commits before merging into main.

questions.text: In the Software Testing Pyramid, which tier of tests should form the largest, fastest foundation of your automated test suite?
questions.explanation: Unit tests are fast to run and isolated, providing the broad base of the testing pyramid.

questions.text: What guiding philosophy defines React Testing Library (RTL)?

options.text: The more your tests resemble the way your software is used, the more confidence they can give you.
Always test internal state variables directly.
All tests must be written in Python.

questions.explanation: RTL encourages testing from the user perspective (querying by accessible roles, labels, text) rather than testing internal state implementation.

questions.text: What query method is recommended as top priority when searching for elements in React Testing Library?

questions.text: When a Super Admin deletes a course in the Admin Studio, why must database cascading deletion rules be executed?
